label: copy phase: digit 0 being output now or next (recall position >= 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original phase or at <DEL>) and only on steps whose input is a repeated token (in_first=0). It tracks the digit 0 in the output stream: out_tok==0 has a 54% firing rate (23x lift) and holds 56% of activation mass, and next_out==0 adds anticipatory firing one step before a 0 is output. The activation ramps up over the 1-2 steps before a run of 0s, peaks on the step that outputs the first 0 of the run, and decays across later 0s in the run. It is weak at recall positions 0-2 and strongest at recall_idx 3-5. Rate goes up with the number of digits in the sequence. The predicate gets dev F1 0.66 (P 0.72, R 0.62) and mass recall 0.82. It misses diffuse low-magnitude firing in sequences with no 0 at all (about 18% of mass), and it gives false positives when a 0 comes early in the copy (recall_idx 2), where the feature often stays silent.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: 0, h, 1, i, f, y; least: s, 3, k, v) and the next token to output (most: 0, j, f, 1, e, z; least: s, 3, k, v); timing cues that raise it most: phase=2, recall_idx=4, recall_idx=3.
